name: User Interviews
description: Conduct deep conversations to understand user needs experiences and pain points through active listening
key_questions: What brings you here today?|Walk me through a recent experience|What frustrates you most?|What would make this easier?|Tell me more about that

name: Empathy Mapping
description: Create visual representation of what users say think do and feel to build deep understanding
key_questions: What did they say?|What might they be thinking?|What actions did they take?|What emotions surfaced?

name: Shadowing
description: Examine real-world context, workarounds, and constraints around how people currently handle the situation
key_questions: Walk me through what happens before and after the key moment?|What clumsy workarounds already exist?|What goes unsaid when people try this today?

name: Journey Mapping
description: Map the end-to-end human experience across touchpoints to spot friction and emotional turns
key_questions: Where does the experience actually begin and end?|Where does momentum drop or anxiety spike?|What earns lasting trust?

name: Diary Studies
description: Have users document experiences over time to capture authentic moments and evolving needs
key_questions: What did you experience today?|How did you feel?|What worked or didn't?|What surprised you?

name: Problem Framing
description: Transform observations into clear actionable problem statements that inspire solution generation
key_questions: What's the real problem?|Who experiences this?|Why does it matter?|What would success look like?

name: How Might We
description: Reframe problems as opportunity questions that open solution space without prescribing answers
key_questions: How might we help users...?|How might we make it easier to...?|How might we reduce the friction of...?

name: Point of View Statement
description: Create specific user-centered problem statements that capture who what and why
key_questions: User type needs what because insight|What's driving this need?|Why does it matter to them?

name: Affinity Clustering
description: Group related observations and insights to reveal patterns and opportunity themes
key_questions: What connects these?|What themes emerge?|Group similar items|Name each cluster|What story do they tell?

name: Jobs to be Done
description: Identify functional emotional and social jobs users are hiring solutions to accomplish
key_questions: What job are they trying to do?|What progress do they want?|What are they really hiring this for?|What alternatives exist?

name: Brainstorming
description: Explore broad divergent concepts across the probability tail before filtering for constraints
key_questions: What are the first three obvious ideas we should discard?|What wild alternative solves the underlying tension?|How can we push this direction ten steps further?

name: Crazy 8s
description: Rapidly sketch eight solution variations in eight minutes to force quick creative thinking
key_questions: Fold paper in 8|1 minute per sketch|No overthinking|Quantity over quality|Push past obvious

name: SCAMPER Design
description: Apply seven design lenses to existing solutions - Substitute Combine Adapt Modify Purposes Eliminate Reverse
key_questions: What could we substitute?|How could we combine elements?|What could we adapt?|How could we modify it?|Other purposes?|What to eliminate?|What if reversed?

name: Provotype Sketching
description: Create deliberately provocative or extreme prototypes to spark breakthrough thinking
key_questions: What's the most extreme version?|Make it ridiculous|Push boundaries|What useful insights emerge?

name: Analogous Inspiration
description: Find inspiration from completely different domains to spark innovative connections
key_questions: What other field solves this?|How does nature handle this?|What's an analogous problem?|What can we borrow?

name: Paper Prototyping
description: Create quick low-fidelity sketches and mockups to make ideas tangible for testing
key_questions: Sketch it out|Make it rough|Focus on core concept|Test assumptions|Learn fast

name: Role Playing
description: Act out user scenarios and service interactions to test experience flow and pain points
key_questions: Play the user|Act out the scenario|What feels awkward?|Where does it break?|What works?

name: Wizard of Oz
description: Simulate complex functionality manually behind scenes to test concept before building
key_questions: Fake the backend|Focus on experience|What do they think is happening?|Does the concept work?

name: Storyboarding
description: Visualize user experience across time and touchpoints as sequential illustrated narrative
key_questions: What's scene 1?|How does it progress?|What's the emotional journey?|Where's the climax?|How does it resolve?

name: Physical Mockups
description: Build tangible artifacts users can touch and interact with to test form and function
key_questions: Make it 3D|Use basic materials|Make it interactive|Test ergonomics|Gather reactions

name: Usability Testing
description: Put a tangible prototype in front of real people without coaching to watch where comprehension or flow breaks
key_questions: What can they test without your narration?|Where do they hesitate or misuse it?|What surprised you most?

name: Feedback Capture Grid
description: Organize user feedback across likes questions ideas and changes for actionable insights
key_questions: What did they like?|What questions arose?|What ideas did they have?|What needs changing?

name: A/B Testing
description: Compare two variations to understand which approach better serves user needs
key_questions: Show version A|Show version B|Which works better?|Why the difference?|What does data show?

name: Assumption Testing
description: Identify and validate critical assumptions underlying your solution to reduce risk
key_questions: What are we assuming?|How can we test this?|What would prove us wrong?|What's the riskiest assumption?

name: Iterate and Refine
description: Use test insights to improve prototype through rapid cycles of refinement and re-testing
key_questions: What did we learn?|What needs fixing?|What stays?|Make changes quickly|Test again

name: Pilot Programs
description: Launch small-scale real-world implementation to learn before full rollout
key_questions: Start small|Real users|Real context|What breaks?|What works?|Scale lessons learned

name: Service Blueprinting
description: Map all service components interactions and touchpoints to guide implementation
key_questions: What's visible to users?|What happens backstage?|What systems are needed?|Where are handoffs?

name: Design System Creation
description: Establish repeatable visual, spatial, and experience patterns so delivery stays coherent
key_questions: Which sensory or structural elements repeat across touchpoints?|What standards keep this coherent as it scales?|What should stay rigid vs adaptable?

name: Stakeholder Alignment
description: Test the concept against decision-makers, partners, or operators who can fund, block, or deliver it
key_questions: Who has to say yes for this to happen in reality?|What evidence convinces them fastest?|Where might commitments fray?

name: Measurement Framework
description: Define success metrics and feedback loops to track impact and inform future iterations
key_questions: How will we measure success?|What are key metrics?|How do we gather feedback?|When do we revisit?
